body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Monday, October 12, and the big overnight item was a robbery at the Dollar Tree on Mount Vernon Avenue where a machete was used — two suspects got away on foot and officers are still working the area. Otherwise it's a cool, clean start: 57 degrees at Meadows Field, air quality good at 44, no weather alerts, and one active fire, the Cyrus Fire, still on crews' boards.

## The Kern Overnight

Dispatch logged 32 incidents overnight, led by six crashes, six medical and overdose calls, and four disturbances and welfare checks. The one that drew the most units was the robbery in progress in the 2600 block of Mount Vernon Avenue, where a machete was used at the Dollar Tree. Two suspects were last seen on foot heading toward the fast-food lot next door, and officers were working the area. If you were near Mount Vernon early this morning, that's what the patrol cars were doing.

Out on the roads, a crash on southbound Interstate 5 north of the rest area left two people ejected from a vehicle. Traffic was held while crews worked, and one patient was flown out while the other went by ground. A vehicle rolled over on northbound Rosedale Highway just north of Jenkins Road; crews checked the area but couldn't find a reported black or blue sedan on the right shoulder. Wasco police handled a crash where the driver tried to flee and was detained — nobody was pinned, and the driver complained of generalized pain. Officers also went to Panama Lane and Pebble Point for a vehicle against a pedestrian, with a person reported down in the roadway on the southbound side.

Deputies were sent to the 2100 block of Lancer Drive, where a caller said her husband and four friends had gone dirt biking and none had returned or answered their phones — crews responded for a possible search and rescue. A woman called 911 from Yuma Way to report she had been strangled, then disconnected; officers went to check on her. Firefighters handled a house fire at a county address, finding several spots inside showing heat but no hazard to anyone, and released units from the call. The evening log also included a domestic disturbance in the 1300 block of Princeton Avenue with a criminal protective order listing the caller as a protected party, a man found unconscious and bleeding on a bicycle at Manchester Lane, and a theft in progress on the 3400 block of Mall View Road reported as five juveniles loading up.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 69 and a low around 49 tonight — a genuinely fall-feeling Monday after that stretch of triple-digit heat. It's currently 57 degrees at Meadows Field. No active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is 44, which is good. Fire crews remain on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire. If you've been waiting to open the windows or get back outside, this is the week for it.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Kyiv says Russian strikes on energy facilities are continuing despite what President Trump has called an "energy ceasefire."** The story comes out of Ukraine's capital as the war grinds on, with officials there saying attacks on power infrastructure haven't stopped. For Kern County readers, the through-line is the same one we've watched all year: instability overseas tends to show up at the gas pump and in grocery prices here at home, and energy infrastructure is exactly the kind of target that moves markets.

**According to 23ABC, Bakersfield's Greek Food Festival closed out its three-day run Sunday at St. George Greek Orthodox Church, and organizers hope to beat last year's crowd of about 8,000.** Co-chair Annette Londquist said they think they'll max back out and go beyond 8,000, though she admitted they never really know until the numbers come in. Volunteer Tanya Alsheikh, who's worked the festival since she was 6, said tiramisu cupcakes, pistachio baklava and chocolate hazelnut baklava all sold out — and they made more this year anyway. For Katherine Rupert, it was a bucket-list weekend decades in the making; she came on her daughter's reminder and planned to try everything.

**23ABC also reports that Kern County is getting relief from record October heat, but El Niño could bring a wet winter to Bakersfield.** The city just logged its third-hottest first week of October on record, with four triple-digit days. Chief Meteorologist Brandon Michaels told viewers an upper-level high that had been parked over the region for weeks is finally moving out, replaced by a strong low and a much cooler pattern — though warmer temperatures could still return later this month. Nancy Banducci of Banducci's Family Farm said the heat hurt business badly, with maybe ten customers on a 102-degree day, but families are coming back now that it's cool. Looking further out, Michaels said El Niño could shape what this winter looks like here.

**KGET 17 reports that a pedestrian died in a hit-and-run collision on Brundage Lane and the driver was arrested, according to Bakersfield police.** The department says the driver was taken into custody after the collision. It's a reminder of how quickly things can turn on our busiest corridors, and why Bakersfield police keep asking anyone who sees a crash to stop and call it in rather than drive on.

**KGET 17 also reports that a new veterans center is coming to southwest Bakersfield, according to the secretary of Veterans Affairs.** Details are still thin beyond the announcement, but the news matters for a county with a large veteran population that has long had to travel for some services. We'll share specifics on location and timing as they're released.

**Bakersfield Now is asking readers to vote on whether they think increased ICE enforcement makes California communities safer.** It's an informal reader poll, not a news finding, but it's a useful temperature check on a question that keeps coming up in local conversation. You can weigh in on their site.

## Something good

The third annual Cultura Fest brought families to Stramler Park on Saturday for a free celebration of heritage — traditional dancing, live music and local vendors — organized by Raices of Kern. Proceeds go to scholarships for students, including first-generation college students. Maria Torres watched her daughter perform traditional Mexican dances and said it reminded her of the celebrations she grew up with, and that without events like this, families simply don't get exposed to those traditions. That's a good note to start the week on.

## Coming up this week

The county and city calendar is busy. Today, the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at noon, and the Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3 p.m. Tuesday brings the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee at noon — the one to watch if you care about road projects, bike lanes or bus routes. Wednesday at 10 a.m. is the Water Board, always worth attention in a valley that lives by its groundwater. Thursday at 5:30 p.m. the Planning Commission takes up its agenda. On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate: United We Dance brings festival energy and an all-night lineup on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour hits the stage October 17, Fortune Feimster brings her "Taking Care of Biscuits" tour October 18, Cults & Classics screens *Psycho* on October 19, and Switchfoot with special guest Anberlin plays the Forever Now Tour on October 21. Pick your night — there's something for just about everyone.

Have a good Monday, Bakersfield. Stay cool while it lasts.
